clock_note.how_to_read: Quote server_fhe_run_s = 2,445.06 s as 'monotonic guest clock', and add that real elapsed time was about 2,650 s. Neither is a benchmark latency (n=1).
clock_note.same_effect_in_other_recorded_runs: present in every recorded run (gaps over 1 s were 10% of the MLP run's span, 19% of the very short LR run, 22% of XGBoost attempt 2); LR/MLP/attempt-1/attempt-2 durations are therefore also on the lagging clock. Cause not investigated (VM clock behaviour under host load is the leading suspect; the Phase 8/9 timings were taken in the same kind of WSL VM and were not re-examined).
clock_note.summary: The guest VM's monotonic clock (perf_counter, used for every recorded duration such as server_fhe_run_s and wall_seconds) ran about 8% slower than real time during this run. Real elapsed time from key registration to the end of the serve stage was about 2,650 s against 2,447 s measured monotonically; the guest real-time clock also agrees with the host's clock (launched about 18:05 IST, finished about 18:50 IST).

comparability_note: single cold request (n=1) on this computer with WSL limited to 5GB; Phase 8's recorded 2,650.6 s is a mean of 5 trials from one in-process run. Same CPU, different protocol: report side by side, not as a speed-up.
known_concurrent_activity: a Windows background download (BackgroundDownload.exe under svchost; purpose not verified, probably an update) started at about 18:38 IST and caused a burst of host paging (about 12-14k pages/s for roughly 3 minutes); the VM's own MemAvailable was unaffected and the run completed
